clue.text: Beauty enthralling feeble husband and Republican 27

definitions.note: refers to the answer at 27 across, a ringleader: someone who leads a flock or group

indicators.note: enthralling means holding captive, so the beauty word holds the next pieces inside it

parts.note: a belle is a beautiful woman
wet is British slang for feeble or ineffectual

explanation.surface: A beauty has captivated a weak husband and a Republican politician too.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the cross-reference: the answer to 27 across is RINGLEADER. A bellwether is originally the belled castrated ram leading the flock.
explanation.definitionFit: A bellwether is the leading sheep of a flock, so figuratively one who leads others, a synonym for a ringleader.

clue.text: Figure cool in tight garment

parts.note: bod is informal for a body, i.e. a figure
ice is something cool, to cool by icing

explanation.surface: A shapely figure looks cool in a close-fitting garment.
explanation.definitionFit: A bodice is the close-fitting upper part of a dress, a tight item of women's clothing.

clue.text: Send back your wicked servant's uniform!

indicators.note: sending something back returns it the way it came, so these letters are read in reverse

parts.note: YR is the written short form of your
evil means wicked

explanation.surface: An indignant order to return a wicked servant's uniform.
explanation.definitionFit: Livery is the distinctive uniform worn by servants of a household or guild.

clue.text: Project unfinished: have publicity job with Princess Fiona?

parts.note: work is a job
to have publicity is to be in PR, in public relations' hands
Princess Fiona in the Shrek films is an ogress

explanation.surface: An unfinished project: a PR job for a fairy-tale princess.
explanation.walkthrough: Princess Fiona, from the Shrek animated films, turns into an ogre at night and marries Shrek, so she is an ogress.
explanation.definitionFit: A work in progress is a piece of work still being developed, an incomplete project.

clue.text: Gathering news, driving supporters meet in state

indicators.note: gathering means collecting in, so the supporters word holds the news letters

parts.note: in golf, a ball is driven off from a tee, so tees are supports for driving
N is short for new, so two of them make news
to see someone is to meet them

explanation.surface: Gathered news says golf fans meet in a US state.
explanation.walkthrough: News is read as plural new: N plus N.
explanation.definitionFit: Tennessee is one of the states of the USA, home to Nashville and Memphis.

clue.text: Highly commend reduction of previous charge?

parts.note: ex means former or previous

indicators.note: a reduction shortens the word, so the charge loses a letter

parts.note: a toll is a charge for using a road or bridge

explanation.surface: Praise for a cut in a previous fee, perhaps.
explanation.definitionFit: To extol is to praise enthusiastically, so to commend highly.

clue.text: Start to eat crackers passed round with this?

definitions.text: Start to eat crackers passed round with this?

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter

parts.note: the first letter of eat

indicators.note: passing round turns the word about, so it is read backwards

parts.note: crackers is informal for mad

explanation.surface: Cheese and crackers handed round at a party.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue doubles as a definition: a cheese one might hand round with crackers.
explanation.definitionFit: Edam is a Dutch cheese, often eaten on crackers, matching the scene of the clue.

clue.text: Red Ken is let loose? Hide!

indicators.note: let loose means set free and scattered, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters of these three words, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Red Ken, the left-wing politician, is on the loose, so hide!
explanation.walkthrough: Red Ken is the nickname of Ken Livingstone, former Mayor of London. Hide is the noun, an animal skin, not the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Deerskin is the skin of a deer, a hide used for leather.

clue.text: Revolting person misrepresented term in EU

indicators.note: something misrepresented is shown in the wrong form, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters of these three words, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A disgusting individual twisted the meaning of a term within the EU.
explanation.walkthrough: Revolting looks like disgusting, but here it means rising in revolt.
explanation.definitionFit: A mutineer is someone who rebels against authority, especially on a ship, so a person in revolt.

clue.text: Phone card returned fitting in pocket

indicators.note: returned means sent back, so the card letters are read backwards

parts.note: a SIM is the card inside a mobile phone
appropriate means fitting or suitable

explanation.surface: A phone card handed back fits neatly into a pocket.
explanation.walkthrough: Pocket is a verb here, to take dishonestly.
explanation.definitionFit: To misappropriate is to take funds for oneself dishonestly, which is to pocket them.

clue.text: One going down who might be saved by the bell?

definitions.text: One going down who might be saved by the bell?

parts.note: reads like a boxer sinking to the canvas; really someone descending underwater
the boxing idiom for being rescued by the round ending; here a diving bell, an underwater air chamber

explanation.surface: A boxer on the way down who might be rescued as the round ends.
explanation.walkthrough: The boxing picture misleads: the bell is a diving bell, which supplies air to someone working underwater.
explanation.definitionFit: A diver goes down under water and could be kept alive by a diving bell.

clue.text: Something to sustain enthusiast: old poetry books?

parts.note: a nut is an enthusiast, as in a fitness nut
rime is an archaic spelling of rhyme, i.e. verse
NT is the New Testament, a collection of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: Old poetry books are nourishment for a keen reader.
explanation.definitionFit: Nutriment is nourishing food, something that sustains life.

clue.text: My lovely ornamental moulding

parts.note: cor is a British exclamation of surprise, like 'my!'
nice means lovely or pleasant

explanation.surface: An admirer exclaims at a lovely piece of decorative moulding.
explanation.walkthrough: My is an exclamation, not a possessive; cor is the British equivalent.
explanation.definitionFit: A cornice is a decorative moulding running round a ceiling or the top of a building.

clue.text: Androcles at the outset is drawn into big cat relationship

indicators.note: being drawn into something puts it inside, so these letters go inside the big cat word

parts.note: a lion is a big cat

indicators.note: the outset of a word is its first letter

parts.note: the first letter of Androcles
taken as written

explanation.surface: Androcles, of the fable, is pulled into a friendship with a lion.
explanation.walkthrough: In the fable, Androcles removes a thorn from a lion's paw and is later spared by it.
explanation.definitionFit: A liaison is a connection or relationship, often a secret romantic one.

clue.text: Address those present perhaps in troop ship with sea raging

indicators.note: a raging sea is wild and churning, so these letters are tossed into a new order

parts.note: the letters of troop ship, to be mixed with sea
the letters of sea join the mix

explanation.surface: A speaker addresses the troops on a ship in a storm.
explanation.walkthrough: To apostrophise is a rhetorical term for addressing someone directly in a speech; 'perhaps' admits that the audience need not be present.
explanation.definitionFit: Apostrophising is turning in a speech to speak to a person directly, such as the people present.

clue.text: Affluent speculator acquiring East German house

indicators.note: acquiring means taking in, so the rich word holds the east letter

parts.note: affluent means rich
a stag is a speculator who buys new shares hoping to sell them quickly at a profit

explanation.surface: A wealthy speculator buys a house in East Germany.
explanation.definitionFit: The Reichstag is the building in Berlin that houses the German parliament.

clue.text: Seller's initial costs having risen not right for seasons

indicators.note: initial means the first letter

parts.note: the first letter of seller

indicators.note: not means without, so the right letter is removed

parts.note: when costs have risen, prices are up

explanation.surface: A seller's prices have gone up, but not for the right seasons.
explanation.walkthrough: Seasons is a verb here: to add flavour to food.
explanation.definitionFit: To spice up food is to add flavour to it, which is what seasoning does.

clue.text: Rotten hobnail boot finally chucked in the event

indicators.note: something rotten has fallen apart, so these letters are reassembled

parts.note: the letters of hobnail, to be rearranged

indicators.note: finally means the last letter of the word

parts.note: the last letter of boot joins the mix

explanation.surface: A rotting hobnail boot was thrown out in the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chucked in' just adds the boot's last letter to the mix.
explanation.definitionFit: The biathlon is a sporting event combining cross-country skiing and rifle shooting.

clue.text: Ancestor, strait-laced, reversed disintegration Self embodies?

parts.note: prim means strait-laced, stiffly proper

indicators.note: reversed means read backwards

parts.note: rot is decay, a falling apart
what something embodies is in it
ego is the self

explanation.surface: A prim forebear embodies decay of the self.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase 'disintegration Self embodies' reads as rot in ego, and that whole string turns round.
explanation.definitionFit: A primogenitor is an earliest ancestor, the original forefather of a family line.

clue.text: Let out and glad to go topless

indicators.note: in a down answer the top is the first letter, so going topless means losing it

parts.note: pleased means glad

explanation.surface: Released and happy to go topless in the sun.
explanation.walkthrough: Let out means rented, as of a flat, not released.
explanation.definitionFit: To lease property is to let it out, so leased means rented out.

clue.text: Accommodates, as it were, men in drunken state?

indicators.note: accommodates is puts up; in a down answer up means written bottom to top, so these letters read backwards

parts.note: puts, as in puts up, gives lodging
OR is other ranks, the ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: A host puts up men who arrive drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: Accommodates means puts up: in a down clue, put the word puts upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A stupor is a dazed, nearly unconscious condition, the kind brought on by heavy drinking.

clue.text: Clique outrageously erotic — bed needs stripping

indicators.note: behaving outrageously means wild, so the letters are thrown about

parts.note: the letters of erotic, to be rearranged

indicators.note: stripping takes off the outer layers, leaving the middle letter

parts.note: the middle letter of bed, once its outer letters are stripped

explanation.surface: A wild, erotic set where the bed needs its sheets taken off.
explanation.definitionFit: A coterie is a small exclusive group sharing interests, which is a clique.

clue.text: Bug found in green sauce Penny refused

parts.note: eco means environmentally friendly, or green

indicators.note: refused means turned away, so the penny letter is taken out

parts.note: lip is cheek, impertinence, or sauce

explanation.surface: An insect was found in a green sauce, and the diner refused to pay.
explanation.walkthrough: Sauce means cheek here, insolence, as does lip.
explanation.definitionFit: E. coli is a bacterium, and a bug is informal for a germ or microbe.

clue.text: King among monied people with time to reap benefits?

indicators.note: among means inside, so the king letter is placed within

parts.note: the haves are the wealthy, as in haves and have-nots

explanation.surface: A king among the rich takes time to enjoy the rewards.
explanation.definitionFit: To harvest is to gather a crop, or figuratively to reap the benefits of earlier effort.

clue.text: Switch must be installed in jet? Spare no expense

indicators.note: installed in means put inside, so the switch word goes inside the jet word

parts.note: a spout is a jet of liquid
a switch is a flexible stick for whipping, and to lash is to whip

explanation.surface: A switch has to be fitted in a jet, whatever the cost.
explanation.walkthrough: Switch is a whip, not an electrical control.
explanation.definitionFit: To splash out is to spend money freely, so to spare no expense.

clue.text: Fabulist initially adopted revolutionary attitude

indicators.note: initially means the first letter

parts.note: the first letter of adopted

indicators.note: something revolutionary turns over, so the attitude word reads backwards

parts.note: a pose is an attitude or affected stance

explanation.surface: A storyteller first took up a revolutionary stance.
explanation.definitionFit: Aesop was the ancient Greek author of fables, so the classic writer of fables.

clue.text: Long to have pressure in tyre at last

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: at last means the final letter

parts.note: the last letter of tyre

explanation.surface: A wish for some pressure in a tyre at last.
explanation.walkthrough: Long is a verb, to yearn.
explanation.definitionFit: To pine is to yearn or long for something.

clue.text: Band's number one songs broadcast with operatic work

parts.note: The Ring is Wagner's operatic cycle

indicators.note: broadcast means put on the air, so the songs word is heard, not spelt

parts.note: lieder are German art songs

explanation.surface: A band's top hit is followed by songs aired with a work of opera.
explanation.walkthrough: Band is a gang here, and number one its chief.
explanation.definitionFit: A ringleader heads a gang or band of wrongdoers, its number one.
